Free tool · 1 minute

Do you file US taxes as a resident?

The IRS counts your days in the US to decide. It changes which income you report and which forms you file. Count your days here.

By JK Accounting Group · About taxes only — not your visa

Built with JuliaFounder · speaks your language

Count your days in the US

Enter how many days you were in the United States in each year. Nothing is saved and no email is needed.

Enter a number of days (0–366).

Enter a number of days (0–366).

Enter a number of days (0–366).

A "day" means any day you were physically in the US, even part of a day.

Takes about a minute.

Your estimate

Your counted days
This year, plus part of the last two years.
The line for residency
183
Reach it (and 31+ days this year) and you usually count as a resident.
Make sure you file the right way — book a free call → A 20‑minute call. No cost, no pressure.

What this means

In plain words — and what it does not mean.

  • The IRS uses a day count. All of this year's days, plus one third of last year's, plus one sixth of the year before. Reach 183 (and at least 31 days this year) and you usually file as a resident.
  • It changes what you report. A tax resident reports income from the whole world to the IRS. A non-resident usually reports only US income. Getting this wrong is a common and costly mistake.
  • This is about taxes, not your visa. It does not change your immigration status or your green card. And some visas, and treaties between countries, can change the answer.

Hi, I'm Julia.

Founder, JK Accounting GroupEnglish · Russian · Ukrainian

"Am I a resident for taxes?" is one of the first questions people ask me when they move to the US. It sounds simple, but the details matter — and special visas and treaties can change everything.

This tool gives you the quick answer. When it counts, I would be glad to check your exact case with you.

Want to be sure you file the right way?

Send us your details and we will check your exact situation — in English, Russian, or Ukrainian. Or book a free 20‑minute call.

  • We check the visa and treaty rules that apply to you.
  • We file the right forms, the right way.
  • A real person who speaks your language.

Prefer WhatsApp? Message us here

Optional. We will use whatever is easiest for you.

Or book a call now

File with confidence, from day one.

We check your status, apply the right rules, and file correctly — clearly, in your language.

Book a free call → See our other free tools

Miami · Fort Lauderdale · Online

General information, not tax advice. This tool uses the IRS day-count test only. Special visas, exempt days, and tax treaties can change the answer, and this is about taxes — not your immigration status. Please talk to us about your situation.
